issue.title: Coalesce relation-index publishes and memoize the task memo
issue.description:
Coalesce event-driven relation-index publishes and memoize the task memo in bob-ledger-tools.

Root cause: every vault or metadata event runs a full publishRelationIndex(), which copies the records Map, rebuilds relationIndexTaskMemo() over every Tasks task, and walks all edges. A post-layout metadata re-index storm (Obsidian upgrade, cache rebuild, large git pull) therefore costs O(events x (records + tasks)) of main-thread work. Coalesce event-driven publishes (e.g. debounce to one publish per microtask/idle turn) and memoize the task memo across publishes within a turn.

task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved OOM-fix plan scoped the change to stopping the startup crash (layout-ready listener registration, Markdown-only reads, unload guard). Publish coalescing is a separate main-thread performance change with its own regression risk, not needed to stop the crash, so it was left out of the fix.

issue.creation_reason: Follow-up from the relation-index OOM fix: per-event full publishes risk main-thread storms after layout.

payload.entry: Resolved by batch-14 phase bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5.5.6.6.6.6.6.6.5 (bob-plugins 7756f51). Event-driven relation-index publishes now schedule one microtask rebuild (scheduleRelationIndexPublish); api.relationIndex v1 reads (generation, ready, outgoing, incoming, labelSuggestions) and relationLabels.rows flush a pending publish so reads never see stale state; the Tasks task memo is reused within the turn. Tests: storm regression (40 metadata events -> 1 publish, 1 memo build, 1 onChange) and read-after-event freshness in scripts/test-ledger-tools-relation-index.cjs. Cost: synthetic 40-file index 27.6 ms uncoalesced vs 0.58 ms + 1.43 ms coalesced; vault-copy storm 196.96 ms -> 140.79 ms. Lander: full npm test 3814/3814 and validate green on master 35bda67; bob-ledger-tools re-synced from master with scheduleRelationIndexPublish present in the vault copy, 0 drift. Known limitation: distinct async turns (scan chunks, target reads) still publish separately; in-app renderer cost was not measured.
